newsitem.title: UK: Diana to back anti-landmine campaign in parliament.
newsitem.headline: Diana to back anti-landmine campaign in parliament.

text.p: Princess Diana is to back a drive for an international ban on landmines by meeting campaigners in Britain's parliament on Wednesday.
Diana is not due to speak at the meeting in the lower House of Commons, but the organisers say her agreement to attend the campaign by the all-party Landmines Eradication Group is a major boost.
Last month Britain's new Labour government promised to destroy all Britain's anti-personnel mines by 2005, after promising to put human rights at the centre of foreign policy.
But the Landmines Eradication Group, which includes members of parliament from all parties, wants to push for a worldwide ban.
Diana, Princess of Wales, who toured war-ravaged Angola in January to meet landmine victims, has criticised countries which trade in landmines and has called for a worldwide ban.

Labour member of parliament Frank Cook, chairman of the all-party group, said: "We need the high profile support of people like the princess to force other governments to follow the British example and ban this disgusting trade in landmines."
Diana will be attending the meeting on the same day her dresses go on sale in New York to raise money for charity.
Auction house Christie's is selling 79 of her dresses with the proceeds going to AIDS and cancer charities.
